access: by application; delivered package version and available components confirmed with the request
maps: Registered OpenDRIVE maps at all three sites

behavior_ssm.principle: relative motion, oriented-box spatial relations, and registered map semantics
behavior_ssm.eligibility: each actor has >=1 continuous second at native recorded speed >=0.5 m/s somewhere in its observed track
behavior_ssm.unit: recording-local directed ego-target x behavior interval
behavior_ssm.distribution_support: >=30 finite/evaluable intervals from >=5 recordings within each behavior-VRU-metric cell

types.name: Following a leader
types.definition: Ego travels behind a same-route VRU while maintaining a roughly steady longitudinal gap.

types.name: Approaching a moving leader
types.definition: Ego closes the longitudinal gap to a moving VRU ahead.

types.name: Approaching a stopped target
types.definition: Ego closes the gap to a VRU that is currently stationary ahead.

types.name: Crossing
types.definition: A VRU traverses ego's path with temporally associated passage.

types.name: Opposing approach
types.definition: An oncoming VRU ahead approaches ego within shared traffic space.

types.name: Completed opposing passage
types.definition: An opposite-direction VRU moves from ahead to behind ego while remaining laterally separated.

types.name: Side neighbor
types.definition: A VRU occupies nearby lateral space alongside ego.

types.name: Ego passing
types.definition: A same-direction VRU moves from fully ahead to fully behind ego, with continuous lateral separation.

types.name: Ego being passed
types.definition: A same-direction VRU moves from fully behind to fully ahead of ego, with continuous lateral separation.

types.name: Corridor entry
types.definition: A VRU moves from lateral space into ego's projected travel corridor, ahead or behind.

types.name: Corridor exit
types.definition: A VRU leaves ego's projected travel corridor toward lateral space.

types.name: Route joining context
types.definition: Ego and a VRU approach from different roads and converge onto a common outgoing lane path.

types.name: Route leaving context
types.definition: Ego and a VRU share an incoming lane path and diverge toward different outgoing roads.

scenarios.unit: one selected motor-vehicle ego with successive or concurrent targets

forecasting.test_scope: One held-out acquisition date at Site C; no claim of universal performance across unseen locations.

request_channel: laboratory application form; GitHub issues are no longer accepted
